t: The Signature Vision: Collective Transport Bots
title: The Signature Vision: Collective Transport Bots
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Collective Transport Bots.
description:
The Signature vision of Collective Transport Bots does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature bot hulls program, charter one: master carrier bots at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale bot logistics manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate load sharing systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Collective Transport Bots becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

t: 2030 — First bot hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
title: 2030 — First bot hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
definition: 2030 milestone on the Collective Transport Bots roadmap.
description:
First bot hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses, farms and formation control construction sites.

What must be true first: the carrier bots results have to replicate outside the lab, bot logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and load sharing operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed carrier bots demonstrations, bot logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting load sharing uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Collective Transport Bots
definition: Estimates Collective Transport Bots readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Collective Transport Bots components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a bot hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Collective Transport Bots Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Collective Transport Bots operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Collective Transport Bots installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 45924 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where carrier bots monitoring, bot logistics redundancy, or load sharing maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Collective Transport Bots Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Collective Transport Bots: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Collective Transport Bots — bots teaming up to carry heavy loads.

Phase 1 — Prove (carrier bots): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (bot logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (load sharing): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (formation control): bot hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and logistics-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
